name: Prešeren Square
description: The central square by the Triple Bridge, with a statue of France Prešeren, Slovenia’s national poet.

name: Congress Square
description: A large square laid out for a congress of European powers in 1821, bordered by the university and the Philharmonic.

name: Metelkova
description: Former army barracks taken over by artists and squatters in 1993, now an independent center for clubs, galleries, and street art.

name: Ljubljana Castle
description: A medieval castle on the hill above the old town, reached by funicular, with a museum and a lookout tower.

name: National Museum of Contemporary History
description: A museum in Tivoli Park about Slovenia in the 20th century, from the world wars to independence in 1991.

name: Faculty of Arts
places: Faculty of Arts, University of Ljubljana
description: The humanities faculty of the University of Ljubljana, Slovenia’s oldest university.

name: Republic Square
description: A large square built in the 1960s and 1970s, where Slovenia’s independence was proclaimed on June 26, 1991.

name: Ljubljana City Museum
description: A museum of the city’s history in a former noble palace, from the Roman town of Emona to the present.
